title: Flow event dispatch: layer hook -> ConnectionHandler -> AddonManager -> addon method
answers: How does mitmproxy dispatch request/response/error events to addons?
Where are HTTP hooks yielded and handled?
How does flow.intercept block until resume?
body:
1. Layers yield hook commands (commands.StartHook subclasses): proxy/layers/http/_hooks.py (HttpRequestHook, HttpResponseHook, HttpErrorHook, HttpConnectHook...), yielded in proxy/layers/http/__init__.py (HttpRequestHook ~348/377, HttpResponseHook ~511, HttpErrorHook ~616/679/713/744, HttpConnectHook ~775).
2. proxy/server.py:ConnectionHandler.hook_task calls handle_hook(hook); if hook.blocking, sends events.HookCompleted(hook) back to the layer.
3. proxy/mode_servers.py:handle_hook takes the flow arg, calls master.addons.handle_lifecycle(hook), then `await data.wait_for_resume()` if arg is a Flow (this implements intercept/resume).
4. addonmanager.py:AddonManager.handle_lifecycle -> trigger_event(event); if first arg is a flow.Flow, also fires hooks.UpdateHook([flow]).
5. trigger_event iterates self.chain in order, invoke_addon inside safecall(); exceptions.AddonHalt stops the chain. invoke_addon uses _iter_hooks: getattr(addon, event.name) over traverse([addon]) (children too), calls func(*event.args()), awaits if awaitable. invoke_addon_sync rejects coroutines.
Note: proxy/server.py also has a separate handle_hook (~line 497) dispatching by hook.name to a handler table (not read in detail). Mapping event.name from hook class (hooks.py) was not verified.
